author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Tim Walberg highlights record tax refund season and new tax relief measures
text:
U.S. Representative Tim Walberg announced on Apr. 15 that this year’s tax season has brought the largest tax refunds in American history, citing the impact of recent legislation known as the Working Families Tax Cuts.
The announcement is significant for working-class Americans, especially those in Michigan’s 5th Congressional District, who are expected to see more money in their pockets due to changes in federal tax policy.
“This tax season, millions of working-class Americans are benefiting from the critical relief delivered in the Working Families Tax Cuts, making it the largest tax refund season in history,” said Rep. Walberg. “Policies like no tax on tips, overtime, and Social Security will help Michigan families pocket more of their hard-earned money, increasing their take-home pay, and boosting the economy. This once-in-a-generation legislation also prevented residents of Michigan’s 5th Congressional District from seeing a 27% tax hike to make life more affordable for families across the district. We will continue to work on reducing costs and delivering vital relief for hardworking Michiganders.”
The One Big Beautiful Bill Act included several key provisions: an increase by $1,500 per family and a permanent doubling of the standard deduction; permanent lower tax rates from previous cuts; elimination of taxes on tips, overtime pay, and Social Security benefits for most recipients; an increased Child Tax Credit set at $2,200 with adjustments for inflation; expanded access to child care; a permanent paid leave credit; broader use of 529 savings accounts for education needs; and a $1,000 savings account established for every newborn child.
Walberg has represented Michigan’s 5th district since replacing Mark Schauer in Congress in 2011 according to Ballotpedia . Before his tenure in Congress began over a decade ago, he served as a member of the Michigan House of Representatives between 1983 and 1999 according to his official biography .
Walberg was born in Chicago in 1951 and currently resides in Tipton at age 72 as reported by Wikipedia . He earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from Taylor University according to his official biography .
